title: It's going to snow, they say
goal: Pass on news in any tense with -(y)mIş: geliyormuş, gelecekmiş, gelirmiş.

intro.text: Other tenses take `-(y)mIş` instead of the past to pass on what you heard: *Yarın kar yağacakmış* (It's going to snow tomorrow, they say), *Ayşe Ankara'da çalışıyormuş* (Ayşe works in Ankara, I hear).

exercises.question: How do you pass on **It's going to rain tomorrow, they say**?

why.1: *Yağacaktı* means **it was going to rain**: a plan or a forecast seen from the past.

exercises.explain: Future + reported: *yağ-acak* + *-mış*: **it's going to rain, they say**.

exercises.label: *çalışmak* + `-(I)yormuş`: I'm working, they say; you're working…
exercises.explain: `-(I)yor` + *-muş* (always u after *-yor*) + the type I endings *-um, -sun, -uz, -sunuz*.

exercises.en: Ali called. He's going to be a bit late, he says.

reject.why: *Kalacak* states it yourself. You're passing on Ali's message: *kalacakmış*.
*Kalacaktı* is **he was going to be late**. For his message about today, *kalacakmış*.

accept: The price of bread is going to go up, they say.
[Apparently|They say|I hear|I heard] the price of bread is going to go up.
[Apparently|They say|I hear|I heard] bread is going to get more expensive.
Bread is going to get more expensive, [they say|apparently|I hear].
The price of bread is going to [rise|increase|go up][, apparently|, I hear].
[Apparently|They say|I hear|I heard] the price of bread is going to [rise|increase].
Bread prices are going to [go up|rise|increase], [they say|apparently|I hear].
[Apparently|They say|I hear|I heard] bread prices are going to [go up|rise|increase].
There is going to be a price [increase|rise] on bread, [they say|apparently|I hear].

exercises.tr: Hava durumuna göre yarın kar yağacakmış.
exercises.en: According to the forecast, it's going to snow tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: Apparently Elif lives in Izmir now.

exercises.text: Dedem çocukken her sabah beşte kalk___.
exercises.en: As a child, my grandfather used to get up at five every morning, they say.
exercises.explain: A past habit you only heard about: aorist *kalk-ar* + *-mış*. *Kalkardı* would be a habit you know first-hand.

exercises.text: Apparently the company has announced the new prices.
accept: The company has apparently announced the new prices.

exercises.explain: Negative *-mi*, *-yor*, then *-muş*: after *-yor* the vowel is always u.

exercises.prompt: Is he coming tomorrow, did he say?

exercises.en: This information isn't correct, it turns out.

exercises.question: Your friend says: *Ali sınavı geçmişmiş.* How does she feel about the news?
exercises.explain: *-mIşmIş* reports a report, often with doubt or irony: **Ali has supposedly passed the exam**.

accept: According to the rumour, the company is going to close.
According to the [rumor|rumours|rumors], the company [is going to close|will close|is closing].
According to the rumour, the company [will close|is closing].
[Rumour|Rumor] has it (that) the company [is going to close|will close|is closing].
There is a [rumour|rumor] that the company is going to close.
